title: When Your Teen Is Doing More Than Their Share of a Group Project
summary: Use a Contribution Ledger to separate agreed work from assumptions, help your teen make one neutral request, and use the school route proportionately when a live group task is at risk.
seo_description: A parent guide for a teen group-project problem: record task facts, make one neutral request, and know when to involve the school before the work is at risk.
release_move: The parent helps separate task facts from assumptions and holds access, wellbeing, and safety duties; the teen makes one usable request and owns their agreed next contribution where able.

core_belief_shift.from: I need to choose a side, contact the school in anger, or tell my teen to carry the whole group project.
core_belief_shift.to: We can identify the observable work gap, make one neutral request, and use the teacher route proportionately if the live task needs it.

book_relevance.reason: Social Playbook Chapter 1 supports the teen-facing move from a personal criticism to a specific usable issue; the parent guide gives a complete standalone response first.

hero.alt: A teen and parent sort group-project notes at a table, focusing on the next practical step.

social_image.alt: A teen and parent sort group-project notes at a table, focusing on the next practical step.
